column1: # KLARA IS FOUND, IN THE FIRST OF THE THREE VOLUMES THAT WERE LEFT — AND THE SURNAME HAS A NINTH SPELLING.
# Landesarchiv Berlin, Standesamt Kreuzberg, P Rep. 510 Nr. 679, Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister 1960,
# page 123, under the FEBRUAR heading. Read at the image 11 October 2026. Work list row 250.

column2: STERBEREGISTER KREUZBERG 1960 NR. 316, died 4 FEBRUARY 1960. The religion column is a DASH — no confession stated. Her neighbours on the page date the month beyond doubt: Lukaczewicz, Erich Max Bernhard, 3., ev., 307 · Lade, Arnold Walter Willy, 2., ev., 313 · *** LEIPSHOLZ, 4., –, 316 *** · Lange, Fritz Franz August, 6., –, 345. Crop at site/public/klara-leipsholz-kreuzberg-1960.png.

column1: *** AND THE SURNAME IS LEIPSHOLZ, WITH AN S. A NINTH SPELLING. ***
column2: read at five times magnification in a clear hand: L-e-i-p-s-h-o-l-z. The archive has tracked LEIBHOLZ, LEIPHOLZ, LAIBHOLZ, LEIBHOLTZ, LEIPOLZ and the OCR manglings; LEIPSHOLZ IS NEW AND IS A REGISTRAR'S OWN SPELLING, not a machine's. It is recorded as the primary reading because that is what the page says.

column1: # ---------------- IS SHE KLARA LEIPHOLZ OF DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58 ----------------
WHAT THE ARCHIVE HOLDS ABOUT THAT WOMAN
column2: LEIPHOLZ KLARA, PUTZMACHERIN, SW 29 DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58 in the post-war Berlin Namenteil of 1957 AND 1959, and gone from every volume after. A milliner in Kreuzberg. No birth date, no maiden name, no death.

column1: WHY SHE IS A STRONG CANDIDATE
column2: *** THE FORENAME IS KLARA. THE BOROUGH IS KREUZBERG — Dieffenbachstraße 58 is in it. AND THE TIMING IS EXACT: she is in the 1959 directory and dead on 4 February 1960. *** Of the twenty-one years in her window, seventeen were cleared by the text sweep and 1959 was read at the image and is empty; she is in the first blind year after her last directory entry.

THE SPELLING IS ONE LETTER DIFFERENT and "geb. Diedring" is a maiden name this archive has never held for her. Johanne Klara may be a different woman of a nearly identical surname in the same borough. This archive published a wrong identification on a name and a place once already — the Bloom mariner — and will not do it twice on a letter.

column1: WHAT SETTLES IT, AND IT IS CHEAP
column2: STERBEREGISTER KREUZBERG 1960 NR. 316 carries the LAST ADDRESS. *** IF IT READS DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58 THE QUESTION CLOSES COMPLETELY *** — and with it the thirty-five-year run of that household, 1924 to 1960. Orderable by number through service.berlin.de. A purchase, and David's.

column1: and the household it would close
column2: Paul Leipholz, Schlosser, at Dieffenbachstraße 58 in 1924 and 58a in 1941, 1942 and 1943; Klara, Putzmacherin, at 58 in 1957 and 1959. One address across thirty-five years and a war. NEITHER IS KIN TO ANYONE HERE ON ANY EVIDENCE, and this does not change that.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IS NOW CLOSED AND WHAT IS NOT ----------------

column2: 1959 read at the image and empty · 1960 read at the image and SHE IS IN IT · 1963-1979 swept by text and empty · 1980-1994 swept and empty. The search that row 250 has been carrying since September is over.

column1: 1961 and 1962 remain unread and are now MOOT FOR HER
column2: two blind volumes, P Rep. 510 Nr. 680 and 681. They would complete Kreuzberg 1938-1994 for the surname and are worth reading for that reason alone — but no longer for Klara, who was dead before either year began. Recorded so that "Kreuzberg complete" is not claimed before it is true.

THE L BLOCK SAT AT PAGES 120-129 OF 271, which is 45 per cent of the way through — the same proportion as the 1959 volume's 144-156 of 321. That ratio has now held across two volumes of this office and is how the next reader should find the band.
